_comment:
Server-side question bank for Group Quiz Mode, built for AWS Cloud and AI Day Hanoi (Sept 29, 2026, JW Marriott Hotel Hanoi). Server picks question IDs per category based on player vote, then assembles the puzzle config for each lock type (see quiz-mode-puzzle-config-example.json). This file is NOT loaded directly by the client.

CATEGORIES (6 total, confirmed 2026-08-24): aws-core-services, agentic-ai, security, vietnam-aws, startups-innovation, cloud-fundamentals. Each category originally had 81 entries (13 numeric, 13 word, 30 mcq, 25 statement) = 486 total. A 5th type, `spelling` (for spelling-lock, added 2026-08-25 when streak-lock was replaced with spelling-lock in the puzzle lineup), was added per category: 6-12 entries each, 54 total, bringing the grand total to 540. spelling entries were sourced by reusing existing `word` entries that pass a safety filter (letters+spaces only, 5-16 letters excluding spaces) — except aws-core-services, which had ZERO usable `word` entries (all are bare acronyms or contain digits/symbols) and needed 10 newly-authored entries using real AWS service names already referenced elsewhere in that category. This is HALF the original 160-per-category (960 total) target for the original 4 types, per explicit scope reduction agreed with the requester due to fact-exhaustion and verification-cost constraints on categories with limited fresh 2026 source material.

SOURCING: entries with a source field were verified via live web search/fetch on 2026-08-24 against official pages (kiro.dev, aws.amazon.com, press.aboutamazon.com, nist.gov, theneuron.ai re:Invent 2025 recap). Entries with _verified:false are well-established general knowledge (AWS service purposes, port numbers, startup/security/cloud terminology) that were not individually re-verified against a live source in this pass but are standard, safe facts. Spot-check recommended before production use, especially for _verified:false entries.

_type_to_lock_mapping.word: word-lock only. Answers here are 3-6 letters, matched against word-lock's per-position reel constraint — NOT the same pool as 'spelling'.
_type_to_lock_mapping.mcq: wager-lock only (streak-lock was dropped from the lineup — see docs/quiz-mode-instructions-engine.md for why).
_type_to_lock_mapping.statement: pillar-lock ONLY, repurposed as True/False sorter within a single category. TEMPLATE FORMAT: {correctValue|wrongValue} slot — the backend, NOT the client, must resolve this by picking index 0 (True) or 1 (False) before sending anything over the wire. See quiz-mode-instructions-backend.md section 3.
_type_to_lock_mapping.spelling: spelling-lock only. Each entry's `answer` is the exact string passed into spelling-lock's `pool` config. Answers CAN be multi-word (e.g. 'Kiro Power', 'Direct Connect') — spelling-lock renders a visible gap between words in the slot layout and strips spaces only from the internal shuffled letter pool, so multi-word answers work fine and are not confusing. Rule applied when curating this array: letters and spaces only (no digits/symbols), 5-16 total letters excluding spaces. See docs/quiz-mode-instructions-engine.md for the length-range rationale.

mcq.question: What is cloud computing, in simple terms?
mcq.answer: On-demand delivery of IT resources over the Internet with pay-as-you-go pricing
decoys: A type of physical server room owned by one company
A method for storing paper documents digitally
A subscription-only software license with no usage tracking

decoys: The physical flexibility of server cables

mcq.question: In cloud terminology, what is a 'Region'?
mcq.answer: A separate geographic area containing multiple isolated data center locations
decoys: A billing category for enterprise customers

decoys: A marketing term with no technical meaning
A country-level division for tax purposes
A single desktop computer used for testing

mcq.question: Why do companies use multiple Availability Zones?
mcq.answer: To improve resilience and reduce the impact of a single data center failure
decoys: To increase their monthly bill intentionally

To reduce the number of employees needed

decoys: From operating expenditure to capital expenditure

mcq.answer: Resources can be provisioned in minutes without buying physical hardware
decoys: Resources must be ordered a year in advance
Only government agencies can access them

mcq.answer: The ability to handle increasing (or decreasing) workload by adjusting resources
decoys: The physical size of the server hardware
A fixed limit on how many users can log in
The number of employees managing the servers

decoys: Because it is required by international law

mcq.answer: Computing hardware and servers owned and run in a company's own facilities
decoys: Any system accessed through a web browser

mcq.question: What best describes a 'hybrid cloud' approach?
mcq.answer: A mix of on-premises infrastructure and cloud services working together
decoys: Using only one cloud provider exclusively

A backup system that never connects to the internet

decoys: A cloud data center owned exclusively by one government
A free service with no billing
A local network only accessible within one office

decoys: You must pay for a fixed amount regardless of usage

It only applies to physical hardware purchases

decoys: The time it takes to ship physical servers

decoys: A marketing term with no real function
A type of physical insurance policy
A tool for designing office furniture layouts

mcq.question: What does 'global reach' mean for a cloud provider?
mcq.answer: The ability to deploy applications closer to customers in many locations worldwide
decoys: The ability to operate without any internet connection
A limit on how many countries can use the service
A requirement to hire staff in every country

mcq.answer: Cost predictability and flexibility compared to fixed hardware investments
decoys: A legal mandate that applies to all industries equally
Guaranteed elimination of all IT staff

mcq.answer: A service where the provider handles operational tasks like maintenance and updates
decoys: A service that requires the customer to build everything from scratch
A service only available to government clients
A physical device shipped to the customer's office

It only applies to small businesses
It refers to the physical size of server buildings

mcq.question: What does 'downtime' refer to in a business technology context?

decoys: The time employees spend on lunch breaks

mcq.answer: Access to fundamental computing resources like servers and storage over the internet
decoys: A service limited to marketing analytics

mcq.question: What does 'software as a service' (SaaS) generally mean for a business user?
mcq.answer: Using ready-made software applications delivered over the internet, typically via subscription
